deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1974 'topologie modérée' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'tame' family F of subsets of a space X. Judging from this page and its neighbours, the axioms are roughly: a)-c) Boolean and closure-type stability (finite unions, intersections, complements; closures of members are members). d) F is generated by a subfamily F_0 of locally closed 'variétés' (regular pieces); the alternative axiom set αβγδ on F_0 is said to be equivalent ('kif kif'). e) A finiteness-of-dimension or descending-chain axiom: every chain of members, each closed and nowhere dense ('rare') in the previous one, is eventually empty. f) Connected components of (locally closed) members are finite in number and belong to F. The preceding pages build F-regular cellular partitions and a canonical one.

§5 'Localisation' asks whether the induced family F_A = {B ⊂ A : B ∈ F}, for A ∈ F, is again tame. This is the analogue of the induced structure on a definable set in o-minimality.

(1) a), b), c) are declared evident. Closure is to be taken relative to A, which follows from closure in X intersected with A.

(2) d) reduces to saying that F_A is generated by its members that are locally closed varieties in A. This is only sketched.

(3) Proof of e) for F_A. Take a chain A ⊃ A_1 ⊃ A_2 ⊃ …, with each A_i ∈ F_A closed in A and A_{i+1} nowhere dense in A_i.
- Claim: cl(A_{i+1}) is nowhere dense in cl(A_i), closures taken in X.
- A_i − A_{i+1} is dense in A_i, hence dense in cl(A_i).
- Since A_{i+1} is relatively closed and contained in A_i, A_{i+1} = cl(A_{i+1}) ∩ A_i. So A_i − A_{i+1} ⊂ cl(A_i) − cl(A_{i+1}), and this complement is dense in cl(A_i).
- The closures lie in F by b), so axiom e) for F gives cl(A_i) = ∅ for large i. Hence A_i = ∅.

(4) f) passes to F_A. It suffices that every A ∈ F has finitely many connected components, each in F.
- By d), A is a finite union of locally closed Z_i.
- By f) these may be taken connected, after splitting them into components.
- Each component of A is then a union of some Z_i, so there are finitely many and they lie in F.

Margin: the same works for A any 'variété' of X, not necessarily in F; F_A then satisfies a)-e).

The next page passes to the sheaf-theoretic 'locally in F' closure F̄ when the open members of F form a basis. It notes F = F̄ when X is quasi-compact.
errors: The transcribed/written 'Ā_i rare dans Ā_{i+1}' must be read as cl(A_{i+1}) rare in cl(A_i); the proof that follows establishes the latter.

Axiom d) for F_A is asserted rather than proved. It needs the notion of locally closed 'variété' to be intrinsic to A, i.e. regular pieces of A are F-varieties of X. This is a gap, filled in o-minimal theory by cell decomposition.
Step e) silently uses that closures of members of F are in F (axiom b) and that e) for F refers to closed subsets of X. This is fine, but implicit.

ideas.what: Induced tame structure on a member A of the family (localisation), with inheritance of the axioms
ideas.modern_name: Induced o-minimal structure on a definable set / restriction of a tame (o-minimal) structure
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5); this localisation lemma is not there

ideas.what: Dimension axiom via chains of closed nowhere dense subsets; transfer from relative closures to closures in X
ideas.modern_name: Finite (Krull-type) topological dimension of definable sets; dim(cl A − A) < dim A
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal dimension theory (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions dimension theory for tame spaces only in general terms

ideas.what: Finitely many connected components, each in F, deduced from decomposition into connected locally closed pieces
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of connected components of definable sets

missed.claim: A 1974 axiomatic attempt at tame topology, phrased as a Boolean family of subsets with closure, local closedness generation, a dimension descending-chain axiom and finiteness of components, with a verified localisation step. This predates o-minimality by about a decade and the Esquisse by ten years. Historically notable but mathematically routine.
missed.quote: §5 Localisation ... considérons F_A = {B ∈ 𝔓(A) | B ∈ F}. Evidemment F_A satisfait a) b) c), satisfait-il aussi d) et e) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck's tame topology programme had a concrete axiomatic form in 1974, close to later o-minimal axiomatics. This is relevant for crediting and for the history of o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemmas are elementary and standard in o-minimal geometry. Their only interest is historical: an early (1974) axiomatic tame-topology framework predating van den Dries/KPS, whose existence in the Montpellier archive is already somewhat known.
transcription_corrections: 'Alors Ā_i rare dans Ā_{i+1}' should mathematically read 'Alors Ā_{i+1} rare dans Ā_i'; the bar over A_{i+1} inserted later ('Ā_{i+1} dense dans Ā_i') is actually the complement Ā_i − Ā_{i+1} dense in Ā_i.

'Pour d), oui[?] prouvons[?] ou fait[?] immédiat que' likely reads 'Pour d), est-ce[?] ... revient à dire que F_A est engendré par (F_A)_0, i.e. par les ∈ F_A qui sont des variétés loc. fermées de A'.
Margin likely: 'On peut travailler dans une variété quelconque A de X, et F_A = {B ⊂ A, B ∈ F}; alors F_A satisfait a) b) c) d) e)'.
'ses comp. connex. sont ∈ F et en nb fini' (not 'comp. connec.').
